calibration.note: Direct thread CPU nanoseconds sampled at stage boundaries; no cycle query, calibration, process scaling or per-item CPU sampling.

coverage_notes: Stage CPU uses GetThreadTimes on Windows or CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID on Linux, directly as nanoseconds; no cycles or calibration. Item-only spans record wall and allocations and do not split parent CPU intervals. Successful monotonic Windows stage endpoints provide bounds plus/minus31.25ms. Missing clocks stay unknown. Independent process coverage and entire ratio bounds retain5% tolerance. Chrome cpu_raw units are thread CPU nanoseconds.
CPU folded stacks use exclusive entered stage segments; uninstrumented threads/work are excluded. Chrome/flame wall traces come from tracing spans.

Same-named nested spans on one thread contribute only their outermost inclusive CPU, wall and allocation interval to the named stage aggregate; call counts and individual Chrome spans retain every call.

Allocator numbers include profiler overhead and nested scopes; peak_live is observed process allocator live bytes on current-thread allocations, not OS private memory attribution. Allocation counting requires the executable to install CountingAllocator.

Windows stage private memory is current process PrivateUsage sampled nominally every 20 ms while named stages are active. Values overlap across stages, include profiler overhead, miss short stages and between-sample peaks, and are not allocations attributable to a stage. Null means no successful sample; failed samples are counted. Other platforms have no stage private-memory sampling.

Stage I/O uses process-wide overlapping windows and includes profiling writes; it is not additive. Explicit attributed bytes/call elapsed/block durations cover only annotated operations; call elapsed includes scheduling and copying and is not blocked I/O. Failed calls can leave partial byte counts unknown. Windows peak_private is process lifetime peak committed private/pagefile usage; Linux private peak unavailable.
measurement_errors: covered/process CPU uncertainty is not wholly within 5%

Report serialization after the snapshot is outside this measurement window.
